## Simple explanation

JavaScript is a programming language that runs in web browsers and on servers.
It is often used to build the interfaces through which people interact with
AI-powered products.

## Technical explanation

JavaScript is a dynamic, high-level language with first-class functions and an
event loop that supports asynchronous operations. Browser APIs and server
runtimes provide access to networking, user interfaces, and other platform
capabilities.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

AI engineers use JavaScript to connect user interfaces to model-serving APIs,
build interactive demos, and implement applications that run in browsers or
Node.js. JavaScript and TypeScript SDKs also make model services accessible
from web applications.

## How it works

In a browser, a JavaScript engine executes scripts alongside the document
object model. In Node.js and other server runtimes, the language can handle
network requests and application logic. Promises and `async`/`await` help
coordinate operations such as API calls without blocking the interface.

## Practical example

```javascript
const response = await fetch("/api/predictions", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ text: "Classify this sentence" }),
});

const prediction = await response.json();
```

This example sends input to an application endpoint and parses the JSON
prediction returned by the service.

## Common misconceptions

- JavaScript and Java are separate languages despite their similar names.
- Code running in a browser should not contain private API credentials; secrets
  belong on a trusted server.
- JavaScript can call model APIs, but it does not by itself provide a model or
  guarantee that inference runs locally.
